title: Transfer of a dualizing complex along a finite ring map
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] for which $B$ is finitely generated as an $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Use $D(A)$ and $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on their one-object ringed sites. Let $L\in D(A)$ have finitely generated cohomology in every degree and be isomorphic to a bounded complex of injective $A$-modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Assume that the scalar-action map $A[0]\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(L,L)$ is an isomorphism. Then $\Omega_B=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,L)$, regarded as a $B$-complex by the action induced from $(b\varphi)(x)=\varphi(bx)$, has finitely generated $B$-cohomology in every degree, is isomorphic to a bounded complex of injective $B$-modules, and its scalar-action map $B[0]\to R\operatorname{Hom}_B(\Omega_B,\Omega_B)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0AX0, lemma-dualizing-finite; all three conditions expanded using Tag 0A7B, definition-dualizing, and more-algebra.tex Tag 0A5S, definition-injective-dimension.

proof.text: Choose a bounded injective representative $I^\bullet$ of $L$, supported in some interval $[a,b]$ with $a\leq b$. By [lem-trf-coinduction-bounded-injective-model], $J^q=\operatorname{Hom}_A(B,I^q)$, with the stated precomposition action and postcomposition differential, represents $\Omega_B$ and is a bounded complex of injective $B$-modules. The action agrees with that of the item because $B$ is commutative: $\varphi(xb)=\varphi(bx)$. Thus $\Omega_B=C_B(L)$ with this specified comparison, proving the injective-dimension conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0AX0, lemma-dualizing-finite, first paragraph; Tag 0A70 for the derived coinduction model.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-coherent-rhom-finite-injective-dimension] with $K=B[0]$ and the given $L$. The Noetherian hypothesis is on $A$, the only nonzero cohomology of $B[0]$ is the finite $A$-module $B$, and $L$ has finite cohomology and a bounded injective representative. Thus every cohomology module of $\Omega_B$ is finite over $A$. Each finite set of $A$-generators also generates as a $B$-module: its $B$-span contains its $A$-span, which is the whole module, by the definition [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. This proves finite $B$-cohomology.

source.place: Tag 0AX0, second paragraph (coherence), and Tag 0G4H, lemma-finite-ext-into-bounded-injective.

proof.text: The ring $A$ is Noetherian and $B$ is a finite $A$-module. The given $L$ has a bounded injective representative and its actual scalar-action map is invertible. Thus [lem-trf-finite-module-canonical-biduality], with $M=B$, gives an isomorphism $\delta_{B,L}:B[0]\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B[0],L),L)$, specifically the transpose of evaluation. All its hypotheses are precisely assumptions of the item.

source.place: Tag 0A7C, lemma-dualizing, canonical biduality proof; more-algebra.tex Tags 066E, 0A67 and 0A69.

proof.text: Write $U:D(B)\to D(A)$ for restriction and use $\Omega_B=C_B(L)$ from Step 1. Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-derived-hom-adjunction] with its rings $P=A$, $A=B$, its $X=C_B(L)$ and $Y=L$. Its general $\Theta_{X,Y}$ clause gives $$U R\operatorname{Hom}_B(C_B(L),C_B(L))\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_A(UC_B(L),L).$$ The underlying-object comparison in [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction] identifies the target with $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(R\operatorname{Hom}_A(B[0],L),L)$. On the Hom representatives from Step 1, scalar multiplication is the chain map $b\mapsto[\varphi\mapsto b\varphi]$ on $J^\bullet$. The cited evaluation-at-$1$ formula sends it to $b\mapsto[\varphi\mapsto(b\varphi)(1)=\varphi(b)]$ into $I^\bullet$, in each degree. This is the canonical evaluation transpose $\delta_{B,L}$ of Step 3; $b$ has degree zero, so no sign occurs. The comparison therefore identifies the actual restricted scalar-action morphism with an isomorphism. By conservative restriction in [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction], the scalar-action morphism is an isomorphism in $D(B)$. Steps 1 and 2 supply the other two conclusions.
